Modi says he forgives protesters who abused him during youth-led demonstrations against exam paper leaks
items.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he wanted to “forgive” protesters who abused him during recent youth-led demonstrations that dealt a rare political setback to his government. The remarks came after the online Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) mobilised large protests in New Delhi and other cities over examination paper leaks, posing the biggest challenge to Modi’s government in recent years. Some protesters featured in widely circulated videos shouting insults at the prime minister have since faced online abuse from Modi supporters as well as police complaints, according to local media reports. Police have also asked social media platforms, including Meta and X, to take down what they described as abusive and manipulated content targeting the premier. “The country and the world witnessed what happened at Jantar Mantar. Some mischievous youngsters hurled vile abuses,” Modi, 75, said in a video posted on Instagram late on Friday. “Words were used that do not belong to civilised society — directed not just at me, but even at my late mother … I want to forgive them.” Modi also said “mistakes made in youth” should be corrected through guidance rather than legal action, referring to the police cases. The protests that began last month were initially sparked by anger over examination paper leaks. But they broadened into a wider expression of frustration over unemployment and governance, culminating in the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Since the protests began, Modi has increasingly used Instagram — the platform on which the CJP built much of its support — to communicate directly with youngsters. Modi’s ruling party has 9.6 million Instagram followers, while the CJP, launched only in May, has more than 26m.

FIFA scraps private investment plan after fierce backlash from officials worldwide
items.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino said on Saturday he has scrapped a plan to allow private investment in the World Cup following fierce backlash from football officials worldwide. “Our purpose has always been — and will always be — to unite and improve,” Infantino said in a statement. “As a result, this proposal will not proceed.” FIFA, world football’s governing body, had floated the plan on Tuesday, saying it could raise up to $4.2 billion based on a valuation of $20bn for a new FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a commercial subsidiary it proposed to run events such as the World Cup and Club World Cup. It said that, if approved, the project could provide each of FIFA’s 211 member associations with a one-off payment of $20 million in early 2027 and increase their funding allocation for the 2027-2030 cycle from $8 million to $20m. The Asian Football Confederation, which represents 47 member nations, welcomed the plan’s withdrawal on Saturday. Any initiative that may impact global football should be “presented and discussed with the Confederations, the FIFA Council, Member Associations (MAs) and other stakeholders in a timely, transparent and meaningful manner,” the Kuala Lumpur-based body said in a statement. The Mexican Football Federation also welcomed the move, saying that “unity among all the Confederations and Federations has been prioritised for the good of football”. Earlier this week, European football’s governing body UEFA said none of its national teams would participate in any FIFA competition “for so long as these proposals remain alive”. The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and North American and Caribbean federation (CONCACAF) also condemned the move. “The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product,” UEFA said in a statement. “No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.” Pressure mounted on Infantino on Friday with the resignation of senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro, who called the idea “a bad deal for FIFA’s member associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game”. South American confederation CONMEBOL, whose president Alejandro Dominguez is regarded as a close ally of Infantino, demanded further information on the “scope, structure, governance and potential effects” of the project. ‘Created divisions’ In the late-night statement announcing the plan was dead, Infantino said the project was conceived as a means of strengthening member associations, and that it would only have gone ahead if a majority supported it. “Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place,” he said. FIFA had tried to fend off the critics, saying in a statement early on Friday that it would continue consultations with member associations and insisting that “nobody is selling football”. But the pressure mounted, and not just within the football community. A day after the European Union praised UEFA for “defending the integrity of the game,” UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Friday that Infantino was “the wrong man” to lead FIFA. The beleaguered Infantino said he would focus now on restoring harmony while continuing to grow the game. “Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support,” he said.

items.title: MOUNTAINEERING: THE LAST DESCENT
items.description: Austrian Markus Kronthaler’s remains being brought down from Broad Peak. Six Pakistani and two Austrian mountaineers collaborated in the 2007 recovery mission | Photo courtesy Georg Kronthaler This piece was originally published on July 5, 2026. In the past few decades, Pakistan’s mountains have become more and more accessible. A better-equipped airport at Skardu, improved road networks and social media exposure have transformed Pakistan’s adventure tourism industry from being engaged by a select few into one that is attracting hundreds of climbers and trekkers each season, to climb some of the world’s most difficult peaks and cross the highest passes. By any metric, Pakistan’s mountain tourism industry and its local mountaineering culture have seen remarkable success in recent years. But the rapid expansion has also led to some catastrophic consequences, and one that mountaineers know all too well: people do not always return. Fatal accidents claim climbers every season, including those with a lifetime of experience and those who are starting out. What happens when tragedy strikes at the roof of the world? When the climbers are still believed to be alive, both ground and aerial rescue operations are launched to find them. However, if they have died, retrieving a body is an arduous task that few attempt. Every climbing season, Pakistan’s highest mountains claim the lives of mountaineers. Bringing climbers down alive is difficult. Bringing back the dead is even harder. Yet a handful of Pakistanis have quietly taken on one of the world’s most dangerous jobs: recovering bodies from above 7,000 metres As commercial mountaineering expands across Pakistan’s highest peaks, some individuals and small teams have found themselves performing a mission for which there is limited institutional support: bringing back the bodies of those who never returned. In a country that lacks a dedicated private high-altitude rescue and recovery service — the army’s aviation unit is the primary agency for such interventions — these missions often become an improvised system of last resort for grieving families. Mural in Skardu commemorating the four mountaineers who lost their lives in the 2021 K2 winter ascent. The bodies of Muhammad Ali Sadpara, John Snorri and Juan Pablo Mohr still remain on the mountain, while that of Sergi Mingote was recovered | By the writer THE RECOVERY THAT CHANGED MINDS Austrian Georg Kronthaler is making mountaineering and skiing safer. He developed the Local Avalanche Risk Assessment (LARA) app and also conducts courses on predicting avalanches. For him, making mountains safer is a personal mission. But his most lasting contribution might be in changing a long-held view. In July 2006, his younger brother, Markus Kronthaler, tragically lost his life on Broad Peak (8,051 metres) in the Karakoram Range of Gilgit-Baltistan. The 39-year-old had successfully climbed the peak, but the mountain was unforgiving. His body lay just a few metres below the summit but could not be recovered. Markus’ expedition was being recorded and Georg could even listen to the final radio messages that his brother sent. “When my brother died in 2006, I couldn’t accept the idea that he would remain up there forever. My mother would probably have waited her whole life for him to come home,” says Georg Kronthaler, speaking to Eos via WhatsApp. At the time, the accepted opinion amongst the mountaineering community was that if one were to need assistance or die in those altitudes, they could not be helped by other mountaineers. High altitude rescues for the living are not only costly, but also far more technical and dangerous than an expedition to climb a summit. For reference, out of the over 340 people who have died on Mt Everest, nearly 200 bodies remain on the mountain. “I wanted my brother’s death not to have been in vain, but rather to bring about a change in the mindset among mountaineers,” Georg says. “The notion that ‘you can’t help climbers who get into trouble at high altitudes, and under no circumstances can you bring deceased people down from there’ no longer holds true.” Georg set about to recover this brother’s body. “Because this belief was so deeply ingrained among mountaineers, I was even threatened with prosecution in Austria before the expedition,” says Georg. “The prevailing opinion was that no human life should be risked to recover a body, since such a recovery was impossible anyway.” Georg Kronthaler credits Asghar Ali Porik from Jasmine Tours in Skardu for helping organise the expedition to recover his brother’s body in 2007. He was joined by mountaineers Stefan Lackner, Paul Kroler and six Pakistanis: Rozi Ali, Mohammed Amin, Mohamad Hakim, Ghulam Hussain, Mohammed Khan, and “Little” Mohammed Hussain. Porik also organised a training programme with Kronthaler in 2011, where they trained Pakistani mountaineers to carry out high-altitude rescues. “[W]ithout the help of the Pakistani high-altitude porters, the recovery would never have been possible,” says Georg. The emotional toll was immense for both Georg and his parents. “Since it was an incredible burden for my parents that I was going to the place where my younger brother had died, I had promised them I wouldn’t climb all the way up to where my brother was,” he reveals. The recovery mission was depicted in the 2008 German-language documentary Grab in eisigen Höhen [Ice Grave], where one of the most heart-wrenching scenes is where Georg sees the body of his brother for the first time, while still on Broad Peak. As the film chronicles, the highly technical mission did not go as smoothly as intended. However, for Georg, the difficulties were worth it. “After all, the main point is not to leave the deceased lying there like a trash bag,” continues Georg. “My youngest son, Dominik, was born at the exact same hour that my brother Markus died. One leaves, another arrives.” Muhammad Hassan Shigri’s death on the Bottleneck at K2 highlighted the ugly side of mountaineering, as dozens climbed over him to reach the summit of K2 | Associated Press of Pakistan. RECOVERING THE UNRECOVERABLE Kronthaler’s expedition demonstrated that recoveries were possible. Nearly two decades later, Pakistani climbers have begun carrying that work forward themselves. Abid Sadpara comes from mountaineering royalty. He is the son of famed climber Hasan Sadpara, the first Pakistani to achieve the combined distinction of summiting Mt Everest and all five of Pakistan’s 8,000-metre peaks: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak and Gasherbrum II. In 2023, Abid was approached for the retrieval of the body of an Afghan climber, Akbar Ali Sakhi, who had passed away in 2022 on K2, at an altitude of 7,200 metres. At first, Karakoram Expeditions (KE), Sakhi’s tour operator, told his widow Karima Sakhi that they would recover his body, but they later refused, saying that it was impossible to bring it down from that altitude. For many families, a burial matters as much as the climb itself. Without a body, grief often remains suspended indefinitely. Karima was determined to recover her husband’s body and give him a proper burial close to his favourite trail in Kabul. After contacting several tour operators, she was connected to Abid, who agreed to attempt a recovery mission. “The first step was assembling a team of experienced mountaineers, which included Murad Sadpara, Sadiq Sadpara, Ali Musa Sadpara, Ali Shigri, Abideen Shigri, Sajjad Sadpara and Ismail Sadpara,” Abid explains to Eos. “The team then went to train at Khosar Gang (6,040m), a ‘technical’ climb in the Shigar Valley and a popular peak for those wishing to train themselves before going on to K2.” After reaching K2 basecamp, they began the process of acclimatisation, climbing higher every day and setting up camp so that their bodies could get used to the height. Sakhi’s body was on Camp 3, just above the Black Pyramid, over 1,500 feet of exposed rock and ice, and it was necessary that their bodies be primed to conduct both the physical and technical aspects of recovery. It also required getting all the other climbers for that day to understand that there was a recovery mission being attempted. “We requested everyone below us that, for the next two days, they had to restrict their movement for any summit push. Once we could get everyone to agree that they would not be making a summit push, our team could finally go and recover Sakhi,” says Abid. Abid’s team attempted the mission late at night. “People climb in very early hours of the morning at around 3am to 4am. Since we were conducting a recovery mission and needed there to be almost no one trying to climb up, we decided on beginning our recovery mission at night time.” They had to chisel around the body to make Sakhi unstuck. “Around 8pm [after they secured Sakhi’s body], it took them seven hours [to get down] till Camp 2 at the [House’s] Chimney, where they rested for a day and then abseiled down to base camp, where a helicopter was waiting for them and the body,” recalls Abid. “When we brought his body down to CMH [Combined Military Hospital] Skardu and it began to thaw, it was so well preserved in the ice that it was almost like he had died only a week ago,” Abid continues. After Sakhi’s body was brought to Skardu, according to Abid, it was handed over to the Pakistan Army, who then took the responsibility of transporting him first to Islamabad and, later, to Kabul. INSIDE THE DEATH ZONE One of the most controversial incidents on K2 illustrates why body recovery has become such an emotional issue. In July 2023, dozens of mountaineers who were attempting to summit K2 walked over Muhammad Hassan Shigri as he lay dying in the snow, trying to ask for help while his body went numb. The chilling footage of the scene sparked outrage in the mountaineering community and public alike, who questioned why no one helped him down to a lower altitude. “At those altitudes, it’s important to realise that people are in an altered mental state,” says Abid Sadpara. “When you are summiting a peak, you don’t stop to help those around you. You only think about survival for yourself.” UAE-based Pakistani mountaineer Naila Kiani agrees. However, she contends that, in Shigri’s case, the summit push should have been delayed. “With the help of four to five climbers, Shigri could have been brought down to Camp 4 [from the Bottleneck] and provided oxygen. He could have been saved,” she tells Eos via WhatsApp. The next year, Kiani was on a K2 clean-up mission — which involves systematically removing refuse from high altitudes and fragile ecosystems. This entails collecting empty oxygen cylinders, ropes, hooks, tools and even bodies. After contact with Hassan Shigri’s widow and children, Kiani organised a mission to bring back Shigri’s body for a proper burial. Murad Sadpara, also on the Ali Akbar Sakhi recovery team, became a part of the mission. Hassan Shigri’s body was on the Bottleneck — regarded as the most dangerous part of the K2 ascent — a narrow corridor between a serac (an unstable block of ice) and a steep drop. Ali Muhammad Sadpara, who was on a summit push for K2, also ended up joining the recovery mission. “I met Murad [Sadpara] and Naila on the way to the summit, where Murad asked if I could also be a part of the team to recover Shigri’s body,” Ali Muhammad Sadpara tells Eos . “We had left Camp 4 at 9pm for our summit push, reaching the peak at 6:30am. While on my way to summit K2, I could see Shigri’s feet sticking out from under the snow,” narrates Ali Muhammad. “On my way back [from the peak], I crossed the body again and then met up with Murad and Dilawar [Sadpara], and decided to go back up 100 metres with them to recover the body. By this time, Zakir and Akbar Hussein [other members of the mission] had also arrived and the five of us then used ice-axes to break the ice around Shigri’s body.” The team then tied his body with rope and anchored it down, first to Camp 4 and then Camp 3, in around seven hours. According to Ali Muhammad Sadpara, since the clean-up mission was operational with its ropes and fixtures on the mountain, this step became easier than what it typically would have been like. (From left to right) Zakir Sadpara, Dilawar Sadpara, Akbar Hussein, Murad Sadpara and Ali Muhammad Sadpara were part of the team that brought down the remains of Ali Muhammad Shigri from the Bottleneck of K2: Murad Sadpara would tragically lose his own life on Broad Peak in 2024 | Alpine Club of Pakistan THE COST OF RECOVERY Recovery missions also raise another question: who pays? Hassan Shigri’s death shows the precarious economic situation in which Pakistani climbers and porters find themselves in. While climbing at high altitudes is an expensive pursuit, poorly paid porters in Pakistan have to train themselves with meagre resources to take on the world’s highest peaks. “Pakistani porters are paid between five to seven lakh rupees [Rs500,000 to Rs700,000] for an expedition that can last for more than a month,” continues Abid. If they use oxygen, the four to six canisters required for a summit can cost up to Rs400,000. “A porter then needs to decide whether to use oxygen or cut down on the money he brings back to his children,” explains Abid. Abid received Rs6 million — approximately USD21,000 — for the whole team and equipment needed to recover Akbar Ali Sakhi’s body, which is much less than what expeditions to climb K2 would cost if undertaken by a foreign mission. In 2024, American publication Outside Magazine reported that bringing down a body from Everest costs $75,000 — nearly Rs21 million. Until 2014, there were just 10 Pakistani mountaineers who had summited K2, Pakistan’s highest peak. Today, over 54 Pakistani climbers have reached the peak of the Savage Mountain. According to Ayaz Shigri, General Secretary of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, social media has fundamentally changed how porters and climbers from Pakistan are perceived. “The reality is that, before, international climbers would not let their high altitude porters summit with them,” Ayaz tells Eos on the phone. But now, with social media and the availability of video cameras, instances of climbers preventing their porters from summiting have become harder to suppress. “This has resulted in such instances going down,” suggests Ayaz. Uproar over Hassan Shigri’s death was also possible because of the video that was shared on social media, which prompted recovery efforts. THE BODIES THAT REMAIN Poor record-keeping has meant that the exact number of bodies left on Pakistan’s mountains is difficult to ascertain. Unless regular clean-up missions take place, most of them will never be recovered. In February 2021, Ali Sadpara, John Snorri, and Juan Pablo Mohr were killed during an attempt to summit K2 in the winter. An attempt by Ali Sadpara’s son, Sajid Sadpara, in July of that year was unable to bring their bodies down, but Sajid marked their graves. As the trio attempted the “last first” — which specifically refers to achieving the first successful winter summit of K2 — bringing their bodies down from their resting place atop the Killer Mountain will be a feat in itself. Until Pakistan develops a permanent high-altitude rescue and recovery service, every recovery will depend on volunteers willing to risk their own lives to bring someone else home. For now, there are no takers for the dead, and for the dozens who are still on the country’s highest mountains, that call may never come. The writer is Managing Editor of Folio Books Published in Dawn, EOS, July 5th, 2026

items.title: L’armée russe a avancé de 1 km² par jour en moyenne en juillet
items.description: L’armée russe a progressé de 1 km² par jour en moyenne au cours du mois de juillet (31 km²), selon les données du groupe d’analystes ukrainiens Deep State. Le rythme d’avancée de Moscou en Ukraine s’est ainsi effondré de près de 95 % en glissement annuel. Au premier semestre , la progression russe a connu un recul de près de 60 %. Ces chiffres confirment les analyses de plusieurs observateurs, qui estiment que la masse et la sophistication des drones ukrainiens ont virtuellement rendu toute offensive majeure impossible. De plus, les frappes ukrainiennes en profondeur compliquent l'approvisionnement des troupes sur la ligne de front, créant des pénuries de carburant, notamment d'essence, qui est essentielle au fonctionnement des générateurs. Des sources ukrainiennes notent également que la qualité, et notamment le niveau de format des nouvelles recrues russes continue de diminuer, ce qui réduit les capacités du commandement à lancer des opérations complexes « Выживает 1 из 15 ». Темпы продвижения армии РФ в Украине резко упали », Радио Свобода , 31 juillet 2026.'> 1 . L’objectif russe de s’emparer d’ici la fin de l’été des bastions de Kramatorsk et de Sloviansk, dans l’oblast de Donetsk, semble d’ores et déjà intenable. L’offensive de printemps-été – qui a été 16 fois plus lente cette année qu’en 2025, selon l’Institute for the Study of War – ne devrait ainsi pas conduire à une victoire majeure pour Moscou cette année. Selon les données de Deep State, c’est généralement en novembre et en décembre que l’armée russe progresse le plus : respectivement 618 km² et 420 km² en moyenne en 2024-2025. Or, il semble peu probable que l’armée russe soit en mesure de tirer profit de conditions météorologiques plus favorables, étant donné son incapacité à contrer les drones ukrainiens. La neige, la pluie et le brouillard, qui limitent les capacités des drones, pourraient offrir des ouvertures aux troupes russes. Ces fenêtres d'opportunité seront toutefois localisées et ne devraient pas permettre de percées significatives. Ces derniers jours, Moscou a intensifié ses efforts offensifs dans le nord de l’oblast de Kharkiv, notamment dans le secteur de Volchansk, ainsi que dans la région voisine de Soumy. Depuis plusieurs semaines, la Russie cible systématiquement les stations-service dans le nord-est du pays, notamment sur l'autoroute qui relie Poltava à Kharkiv, l'un des principaux axes logistiques de la région vers Kiev. L’article L’armée russe a avancé de 1 km² par jour en moyenne en juillet est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Le corps illibéral de l’idéologie vécue
items.description: Tout l’été, le Grand Continent restera en mouvement. Chaque jour, nous vous apporterons où que vous soyez des idées que vous ne trouverez nulle part ailleurs (mais qui seront partout à la rentrée), des textes introuvables ou rafraîchissants avec nos Dimanches . Pour les recevoir directement dans votre boîte mail et soutenir cet élan, pensez à vous abonner à la revue Le 23 juin 2026, dans la cour du musée des Archives nationales, un jeune homme de vingt ans ouvre le défilé printemps-été 2027 de la marque californienne 424. Il s'appelle Braden Peters, mais un peu plus d’un million de personnes le suivent en ligne sous le nom de Clavicular , un pseudonyme emprunté à l'os que sa communauté fétichise, la clavicule, dont la largeur est censée mesurer la virilité. Clavicular incarne le looksmaxxing ou, littéralement, la maximisation de son apparence. Ce mouvement né au début des années 2010 dans les forums incels , des communautés d'hommes « célibataires involontaires » qui imputent aux femmes leur misère affective. Ses diffusions en direct sur la plateforme Kick lui rapportent environ 100 000 dollars par mois. Comment comprendre qu’une figure marginale, née des forums incels ouvre un défilé à Paris ? La tentation est grande d'y voir un scandale de mode de plus, une provocation calculée dans une industrie qui en a vu d'autres. Ce serait passer à côté de l'essentiel. Défilé de la marque californienne 424, dans la cour du musées des Archives nationales. Paris, le 23 juin 2026. Le moment Clavicular révèle la manière dont l’illibéralisme se banalise aujourd’hui : moins par l’adhésion à une doctrine que par des pratiques, des images et des normes du quotidien. La hiérarchie masculine est devenue une expérience vécue avant d’être une conviction politique. La mode, l’un des espaces où cet illibéralisme banal acquiert prestige et désirabilité. Looksmaxxing et l’esthétique de la hiérarchie La cosmologie du looksmaxxing est d'une brutalité limpide : l'apparence détermine la désirabilité, donc le statut. Qui est beau est souverain ; qui est laid est condamné. La seule issue s'appelle l'« ascension », devenir plus beau, donc plus puissant. Il existe une version présentable, le softmaxxing (on s’occupe de régime, de musculation, de coupe de cheveux stratégique), et une version radicale, le hardmaxxing : à base de chirurgie, hormones, en assumant des risques biomédicaux. Clavicular appartient à cette seconde école : il s'injecte de la testostérone depuis ses quatorze ans, se dit stérile à force d'anabolisants et recommande à ses spectateurs de se frapper la mâchoire au marteau pour la densifier, une pratique que sa communauté appelle tout simplement… bonesmashing . Les criminologues Anda Iulia Solea et Lisa Sugiura ont montré comment, sur TikTok, des contenus issus de la sphère incel se rebaptisent pour échapper plus facilement à la modération : le terme stigmatisé d’« incel » cède la place à des catégories apparemment plus neutres, comme « Sub5 » Digital subcultural diffusion theory : rebranding the incel ideology through Looksmaxxing, Sub5s and the PSL scale », Crime, Media, Culture : An International Journal , 16 novembre 2025. Voir aussi, des mêmes autrices, « Mainstreaming the Blackpill : Understanding the Incel Community on TikTok », European Journal on Criminal Policy and Research, 2023. Le concept de « normiefication », qu’elles appliquent à ce corpus, est emprunté à Daniël de Zeeuw et alii (2020).'> 2 . L'idéologie blackpill , cette vision selon laquelle l’apparence condamnerait biologiquement certains hommes à l’échec sexuel et justifierait leur ressentiment envers les femmes, se reconditionne en conseils d’auto-amélioration, en surface moins extrêmes. Les deux chercheuses décrivent ce processus de « normiefication » comme une rampe d’accès vers des contenus plus durs. Clavicular est accompagné pendant son séjour à Paris par un autre Looksmaxxeur qui se fait appeler « Prince de Paris ». Avec son surnom, ses cheveux plaqués et ses costumes, il joue sur l'imaginaire aristocratique de Paris, associé au chic, à la mode et au luxe. Le rejet et la controverse suscités par sa présence à Paris ont contribué à attirer l'attention sur le voyage de Braden Peters et sur l'événement de 424, et deviennent partie intégrante du spectacle numérique. Avec son surnom, ses cheveux plaqués et ses costumes, il joue sur l'imaginaire aristocratique de Paris, associé au chic, à la mode et au luxe. Le rejet et la controverse suscités par sa présence à Paris ont contribué à attirer l'attention sur le voyage de Braden Peters et sur l'événement de 424, et deviennent partie intégrante du spectacle numérique. Clavicular en est moins le théoricien que le véhicule idéal, précisément parce qu’il traite cet univers comme une question de visibilité plutôt que comme une doctrine. Braden Peters n'est pas un idéologue. Interrogé sur ses convictions, il laisse entendre que ses choix obéissent aux opportunités financières et médiatiques Inside Clavicular's Thirsty Tour of New York City », GQ , 19 février 2026.'> 3 . La politique, dans le lexique de sa communauté, est une affaire de jesters , de bouffons. Et pourtant : on l'a filmé en janvier dans une boîte de Miami, chantant « Heil Hitler » de Kanye West, figure majeure de la provocation antisémite en ligne, aux côtés d’ Andrew Tate , influenceur masculiniste radical, et du suprémaciste blanc Nick Fuentes Nick Fuentes, Andrew Tate and other right-wing influencers filmed singing Ye's 'Heil Hitler' at Miami nightclub », Jewish Telegraphic Agency , 20 janvier 2026.'> 4 . Il avait d’ailleurs confié au New York Times Handsome at Any Cost », The New York Times , 13 février 2026.'> 5 que son intérêt pour le looksmaxxing venait, à l'origine, du désir d'influencer politiquement les autres en devenant plus beau Looks Aren’t Everything ? Clavicular Begs to Differ », The New York Times , février 2026.'> 6 . Il faut donc prendre au sérieux ce déni du politique, car il est lui-même une modalité politique. Quand un adolescent bâtit une audience sur la hiérarchie, l'humiliation, la rareté sexuelle et des canons de beauté racialisés, il fait de la politique, qu'il le revendique ou non. « L'échelle PSL » pick-up artists ), PUAHate glisse rapidement vers un déterminisme radical de l'apparence. Elliot Rodger, auteur de la tuerie d'Isla Vista (Californie) en mai 2014, y était actif, et le forum ferme au lendemain du massacre. Sluthate prend immédiatement sa suite, avant que Lookism.net, lancé en 2015, ne systématise l'« échelle PSL » : une notation de l'attractivité masculine, de 0 à 10, présentée comme objective. Après la fermeture de Lookism, fin 2021, les forums looksmax en ont perpétué l'usage et assuré la diffusion jusque sur TikTok et YouTube. Sur cette généalogie, voir Solea et Sugiura, art. cité.'> 7 , qui prétend noter objectivement l’attractivité physique, privilégie en effet explicitement des traits associés à un idéal européen. Le substrat eugéniste et misogyne travaille d'autant mieux qu'il se présente comme du développement personnel. Vidéo d'une soirée dans une boîte de nuit, diffusée en direct sur le compte Kick de Clavicular. Miami, 17-18 janvier 2026. Reste un paradoxe qui explique le succès de Clavicular : sa sincérité. Contrairement aux biohackers de la Silicon Valley qui drapent leurs protocoles dans la rhétorique de la santé et de la longévité, Clavicular annonce ses fins sans fard : domination et désirabilité. Cette brutalité devient une forme d’authenticité lorsqu’il filme ses injections, raconte ses opérations et ses convalescences. En avril, lorsqu’il s’effondre en direct dans un restaurant de Miami après une overdose présumée, devant des milliers de spectateurs, l’accident lui-même entre dans le spectacle. Car le contenu n’est pas seulement le résultat de la transformation, mais le processus lui-même, y compris lorsqu’il déraille. Une plainte déposée fin avril devant la justice de Floride par Aleksandra Mendoza, recrutée à seize ans pour devenir, selon elle, « le visage féminin du looksmaxxing », rappelle que ce théâtre de l’optimisation peut faire des victimes bien réelles A Female Looksmaxxer Is Suing Clavicular for Alleged Battery », Wired , 29 avril 2026.'> 8 . Elle accuse Peters de l’avoir exploitée, d’avoir eu avec elle des rapports non consentis et de lui avoir injecté en direct, sans qualification médicale, un produit destiné à dissoudre les graisses. Peters nie ces accusations, qui restent à ce stade non jugées. Remilia, ou la réaction devenue avant-garde Le passage de Clavicular sur les podiums n'est pas une excentricité isolée. Son premier défilé, en février à New York, pour la créatrice Elena Velez, était organisé en collaboration avec Remilia Corporation, le laboratoire le plus abouti de l'esthétisation réactionnaire contemporaine. Remilia est un collectif d'art numérique fondé en 2021 par un homme opérant sous le pseudonyme féminin de Charlotte Fang, issu d'un forum réunissant diplômés et décrocheurs d'écoles d'art. Sa création phare, les Milady, est une collection de dix mille avatars vendus sous forme de NFT — ces certificats de propriété numérique qui ont fait la spéculation de l'après-Covid. Dessinés dans un style « neochibi », du nom des figurines d'anime à grosse tête et grands yeux, ces personnages empruntent leurs looks aux tribus de rue du Tokyo des années 2000 — gyaru au bronzage artificiel, lolita en robes à froufrous, excentriques du quartier de Harajuku : autant de sous-cultures où l'identité passe entièrement par le style. La collection a atteint une valorisation de plus de 150 millions de dollars et engendré un empire : cryptomonnaies parodiques ( meme-coins ), marque de compléments alimentaires, agence d'influenceurs, label musical, revue trimestrielle de critique d'art en ligne Inside Remilia Corporation, the anti-woke collective behind the doomed Milady Maker NFT », Fast Company , 21 juin 2022.'> 9 . Cette prolifération commerciale n'est pas un à-côté : elle est, aux yeux du collectif, l'œuvre elle-même. Remilia se théorise comme un « conglomérat planétaire art-industriel », une « corporation-comme-œuvre-d'art », et se place dans une double filiation : la Factory d'Andy Warhol, qui avait fait de l'atelier une entreprise et de l'entreprise un geste artistique, et Bernadette Corporation, collectif new-yorkais des années 1990-2000 qui parodiait les codes de la marque de mode pour en faire un médium. L'idée est la même, portée à l'échelle d'internet : tout — les ventes, la spéculation, la communauté, le marketing — fait partie de l'œuvre Remilia .'> 10 . Sous le vernis conceptuel, la généalogie est explicite. Au cœur de l'approche de Remilia, se trouve la pensée de Nick Land , philosophe britannique néo-réactionnaire autoproclamé, auteur de The Dark Enlightenment , dont l'accélérationnisme irrigue depuis dix ans certains milieux de la Silicon Valley Les Lumières sombres. Comprendre la pensée néoréactionnaire , Paris, Gallimard, coll. « Bibliothèque de géopolitique », 2026.'> 11 . Les multiples rejets qu'il subit à Paris font l'objet de clips viraux, partagés aussi bien par ses fans que par ses détracteurs. La logique du looksmaxxing pousse à des comparaisons constantes avec d'autres hommes afin d’établir une hiérarchie. Un influenceur français insulte ici Clavicular de « tête de paf » à la suite d'une confrontation tendue. En 2022, la révélation que Charlotte Fang avait auparavant opéré sous le pseudonyme de Miya, associé à des publications racistes, homophobes et antisémites ainsi qu’à des communautés en ligne extrêmes, aurait pu sceller le sort du collectif. Il n'en fut rien : la valeur des Milady a fini par rebondir au-delà de ses niveaux d'avant-scandale, et l'identité « post-cancelled » est devenue le mythe fondateur de la communauté. Trois mois après l'affaire, une collection dérivée, commercialisée sous la bannière d'une « esthétique réactionnaire schizophrénique », dépassait les ventes de l'originale. La consolidation politique est venue ensuite. À la veille de la seconde investiture de Donald Trump, Remilia était le sponsor principal du Coronation Ball, le grand bal de la mouvance, dont l'orateur vedette était Steve Bannon Why young MAGA supporters are flocking to Remilia », The Spectator , 8 février 2025.'> 12 . Après son discours, un artiste proche du collectif est monté à la tribune pour exposer le projet de Remilia : refaire le monde, un mème à la fois. Les observateurs qui y cherchent l'intérêt matériel — une régulation plus favorable aux crypto-monnaies, par exemple — ne voient qu'une partie du tableau. L'alignement est aussi, voire surtout, esthétique : un mouvement politique défini par ses images virales rencontre un collectif qui a fait de la circulation mémétique un art. La sociologie de Remilia achève le tableau. Le collectif a explicitement recruté des outsiders : étudiants en mode, catholiques en ligne, cosplayeurs, et figures du Dimes Square à New York, cette scène artistique et médiatique du Lower East Side new-yorkais qui mêle avant-garde, post-ironie et rejet du progressisme culturel. C'est l'accélérationnisme landien traduit en marque de style de vie participative. Le problème des idéologies vécues Il reste à comprendre pourquoi la mode. Elena Velez, demi-finaliste du prix LVMH en 2024 Elena Velez sur le site du prix LVMH.'> 13 et longtemps saluée pour ses corsets métalliques et son travail de construction, a progressivement troqué le stylisme au sens strict contre le rage-bait , c’est-à-dire une stratégie de provocation pensée pour transformer l’indignation en visibilité. Son défilé de février, explicitement consacré au looksmaxxing , réunissait au premier rang des figures de l’extrême droite et de la droite en ligne et faisait défiler, aux côtés de Clavicular, une influenceuse associée à la maigreur extrême. Quelques mois plus tôt, en mars lors de la Fashion Week parisienne, Marilyn Manson, icône du shock rock américain des années 1990, aujourd’hui visé par plusieurs accusations d’abus, ouvrait le défilé d’Enfants Riches Déprimés (ERD), marque de luxe californienne au nom français qui transforme l’imagerie punk, le nihilisme et la provocation en signes de distinction The frozen radicality of Enfants Riches Déprimés' FW26 », nss magazine , 16 mars 2026.'> 14 . Défilé de la marque californienne de luxe Enfants Riches Déprimés lors de la Fashion Week, à la Maison de la Chimie. Paris, 8 mars 2026. Lire ces choix comme de simples provocations à but commercial serait une erreur. Ils montrent d’abord que la culture est devenue un espace central de circulation et de normalisation des valeurs illibérales, bien au-delà des partis et des discours politiques. La culture du corps en constitue une forme particulièrement efficace : en agissant sur les images et les normes de beauté, elle rend ces hiérarchies sensibles et désirables et l'économie de l’attention vient renforcer la spirale. La mise en marché du corps n’est évidemment pas nouvelle : les femmes sont depuis longtemps soumises à des normes qui font de la beauté un critère de valeur. Ce qui change, c’est son extension explicite aux hommes. La beauté masculine devient une ressource de pouvoir au moment où les anciens marqueurs de la virilité comme le salaire, la profession, la capacité à faire vivre une famille sont moins accessibles, moins stables ou moins distinctifs. La difficulté à réinventer la masculinité crée ainsi un terrain fertile pour un credo illibéral qui promet de restaurer la hiérarchie en la réinscrivant dans le corps. Le looksmaxxing est exemplaire parce qu’il n’exige aucune adhésion doctrinale : c’est d’abord une pratique : des routines, des métriques et des transformations corporelles. C’est en ce sens qu’il faut parler d’idéologie vécue : les convictions ne précèdent pas les pratiques ; elles se forment à travers elles. Braden Peters émet de nombreuses remarques sur le nombre de personnes de couleur à Paris lors de la Fête de la musique, le 21 juin, allant jusqu'à comparer Paris à un « ghetto ». Ses streams sont régulièrement le véhicule de remarques racistes destinées à provoquer la controverse. Les influenceuses et mannequins dont s'entoure Clavicular sont régulièrement la cible de remarques dégradantes et misogynes de la part de son chat. Ici la mannequin Adelaide Pali est accusée d'être transgenre, une névrose récurrente des néoconservateurs américains. Ici la mannequin Adelaide Pali est accusée d'être transgenre, une névrose récurrente des néoconservateurs américains. Le looksmaxxing apprend à voir le monde comme une hiérarchie, avant même de fournir les mots qui permettraient de la justifier. Le moment doctrinal peut ensuite survenir, ou non, mais l’idéologie est déjà présente, ancrée dans les gestes. On peut dès lors parler d’illibéralisme banal, en détournant la notion de « nationalisme banal » forgée par Michael Billig 15 . Il ne s’agit pas d’un illibéralisme qui se proclame, mais d’un illibéralisme incorporé, qui se reproduit moins par la persuasion que parce qu’il fait sens commun. Sous-estimer la puissance d’attraction de cette esthétique serait une erreur dangereuse. L’illibéralisme ne progresse pas seulement par les idées qu’il défend, mais par les images qui rendent ses hiérarchies désirables. L’article Le corps illibéral de l’idéologie vécue est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Is Maryam bridging gap between PML-N legislators and admin?
items.description: LAHORE: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has begun meeting PML-N lawmakers on a regular basis to hear their concerns and address issues being faced by their constituents, apparently in an attempt to bridge a growing gap between the party’s legislators and the administrative machinery in the province. On Friday, PML-N MPAs from Bahawalnagar called on the CM and discussed the prevailing political situation, development projects in their constituencies and public issues. The meeting was part of a renewed effort by Ms Nawaz to engage with the party’s lawmakers more frequently. The PML-N legislators from Mandi Bahauddin had also met her over a week ago. CM’s ‘preference for bureaucracy’ has caused resentment among lawmakers The chief minister has been finding it difficult to regularly meet party lawmakers since assuming office in February 2024 because of her demanding schedule and extensive administrative engagements. However, the move to hold more frequent meetings comes against the backdrop of complaints among PML-N MPAs, particularly those representing rural constituencies, that the bureaucracy and police are not giving them importance when they approach them to resolve problems faced by their voters. Soon after taking charge as the CM, Maryam Nawaz had made it clear to the party’s lawmakers that, unlike the practice in the past, they would have no role in civil, administrative or police postings and transfers. The policy was intended to promote merit and professionalism in the provincial administration and prevent political interference in appointments. But it has also caused some unease among PML-N lawmakers, who say that while they do not necessarily want to dictate transfers and postings, they expect government officials to listen to them when they raise “genuine public grievances”. “What most PML-N MPAs want is that the police and bureaucracy give them respect in their constituencies where they go for redress of grievances of their voters. If the chief minister does not bother about them and gives preference to the bureaucracy over them, certainly they will be hurt,” a senior PML-N leader from Punjab told Dawn . He said the issue had been discussed within the party and Ms Maryam had been advised to establish a regular interaction with lawmakers so that their concerns could be heard directly by her. “There may be some ambitious lawmakers who want to run the administrative affairs of their constituencies, but most of them just want respect,” he said. According to the PML-N leader, elected representatives are under considerable pressure from constituents, particularly in the rural areas, who approach them over issues, ranging from policing and land disputes to municipal services, development schemes and other matters involving government departments. “When an MPA takes a complaint to a district officer or a police official and is not given due importance, he faces the anger of his voters. The lawmakers want the chief minister to understand this problem,” he said. The leader said the chief minister’s decision to meet lawmakers more frequently could help address the sense of alienation among some party legislators without compromising her policy of keeping political influence away from postings and transfers. He added that, given the current political environment, Ms Maryam was expected to continue meeting PML-N MPAs and listening to their grievances. The Punjab government, however, maintains that the CM’s policy of merit-based appointments is deliberate and represents a departure from the traditional practice of political interference in the bureaucracy and police. Punjab Information and Culture Minister Azma Bokhari had previously told Dawn that all appointments were now being made strictly on merit and that there was no room for political influence by ruling-party lawmakers or other individuals. Published in Dawn, August 1st, 2026

items.title: El Gobierno admite que no vio venir la crisis de Ceuta: “Si hubiéramos tenido información, no habrían entrado 50.000 en 24 horas”
items.description: El Gobierno no vio venir la crisis de Ceuta. “Es una evidencia que no teníamos información. Si la tienes, no entran 50.000 personas de la forma en que lo han hecho en 24 horas”, reconoce un alto miembro del Ejecutivo. La dimensión de los incendios en el centro y oeste del país, que obligaron además al confinamiento o evacuación de casi 100.000 personas, acaparó durante una semana la atención de La Moncloa y de varios ministerios, entre ellos el de Interior. En medio de la tormenta de fuego, la frontera con Marruecos no preocupaba. No se tuvieron en cuenta las señales de alerta, como los avisos del presidente autonómico, el popular Juan Jesús Vivas, o los primeros informes de la Guardia Civil que apuntaban a un repunte, poco significativo en un primer momento, de las entradas a nado de migrantes irregulares. “Esos días nadie hablaba de Ceuta. Había una lluvia fina de entradas y estábamos pendientes, hasta que prácticamente de un día para otro reventó”, reconoce otro miembro del Ejecutivo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ceuta, una ciudad patas arriba: “Nos vamos porque no hay comida, no nos venden leche para la niña”
items.description: Un triste ejército de pantalones rotos, chancletas disparejas, piernas vendadas y cabezas cubiertas con camisetas sigue una marcha cansina bajo el sol, camino de la frontera con Marruecos. Regresan vencidos. Su aventura ha sido un fracaso. Decenas de miles de inmigrantes llegados en aluvión el jueves desde Marruecos a Ceuta por el mar hicieron ayer el camino de vuelta, sin risas, sin vivas a España, sin ganas. Por la carretera, flanqueada de militares que les apremian el paso, viene cansado un joven matrimonio. El padre carga a una niña de tres años. Apenas 24 horas antes estaban braceando en el mar con la criatura bien sujeta al flotador, una peligrosa travesía que ha dejado decenas de cadáveres en las playas del Tarajal. Y todo para nada. “Nos vamos porque no hay comida, tenemos dinero, pero no nos venden, no hay leche para la niña, todo está cerrado. Y nos han enseñado cuchillos y tirado piedras. Solo queríamos un futuro para mi hija”, cuenta la mujer entre la rabia y la resignación. Nabil tiene 30 años y conduce un Uber en Marruecos y ella, Wisal, ha cumplido 23 criando a una niña que padece de asma. Con todas esas dificultades, más vale desandar el camino. Esta vez será más sencillo, las puertas de España están abiertas y las de Marruecos también. Los centenares de flotadores se acumulan en las instalaciones fronterizas de la Guardia Civil o navegan sin dueño. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Sin recursos para atender a los menores en Ceuta: “Veníamos avisando de que estaba pasando algo, pero no hicieron caso”
items.description: El sudor se mezcla con las lágrimas en el rostro de Malak, una chica de 14 años que lleva un pie vendado. La adolescente, vestida con una camiseta de fútbol y un pantalón corto, cuenta desconsolada que le duele mucho el tobillo que se torció mientras cruzaba a Ceuta por las rocas desde la costa marroquí de Castillejos hace dos días con su hermano Zakariyya, de su misma edad. “Quiero ir al médico”, pide desconsolada. Los hermanos, oriundos de la población costera de Rincón (M’diq), a 23 kilómetros al sur de Ceuta, se han cansado de esquivar a los militares que este viernes por la tarde pastoreaban a miles de hombres, muchos de ellos jóvenes y también algunas mujeres, en dirección a la frontera. Al igual que una decena de chicos que regresaba en torno a las seis de la tarde a su país, aseguran que han intentado acudir a los centros de menores, que la ciudad les diera cobijo, pero solo encontraron saturación y rechazo. Dicen que no han comido. Algunos, que solo han bebido agua. Con la ropa manchada, cansados, caminan hacia la frontera. Algunos cojean. “Nos hemos subido al monte huyendo y nos hemos caído rodando. Los militares nos están echando”, relata Malak exaltada. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mapas y gráficos para entender qué ha pasado en Ceuta: la entrada y salida de casi 50.000 personas en 48 horas
items.description: La mayor oleada de llegadas a Ceuta desde Marruecos ha durado menos de 48 horas. Desde el jueves han entrado unas 50.000 personas ante la inacción de las fuerzas de seguridad marroquíes: las autoridades cifraban en 25.000 los cruces el jueves; 40.000 el viernes por la mañana y 50.000 al mediodía. Pero a lo largo del viernes, según el Ministerio del Interior, la mayoría, unas 48.300 personas, ya había vuelto a Marruecos. Al menos 57 migrantes han muerto, en uno de los acontecimientos más letales en una frontera española. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Priscilla Presley: “Estar al lado de Elvis fue una auténtica lección de vida”
items.description: La cita se celebra cada año, pero el escenario y los protagonistas van cambiando. Esta vez es jueves, 30 de julio, y la temperatura invita a sacar un abanico, aunque no puede hacer mucho más que marear el aire del baño turco en el que se ha convertido Mallorca este verano . El bar del hotel Hilton Mallorca Galatzó, en una zona privilegiada de Calvià, está cerrado al público, que cada poco curiosea a través de los cristales por el trajín de cámaras fotográficas y de vídeo que se mueven de un lado a otro del vestíbulo. Dentro del bar, pertrechada por varios asesores de su equipo, se encuentra Priscilla Presley (Nueva York, 81 años), esposa del rey del rock primero y exesposa después, a pesar de que nunca se separaron del todo. Una mujer delgada, de voz delicada y de tez muy blanca que contrasta con su pelo rojo, color del vestido que llevará en la fiesta posterior. Se levanta inmediatamente para saludar. “Estuve en Mallorca en los años sesenta, pero no la recuerdo así porque era muy joven”, dice casi en un susurro. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El rayo verde, un fascinante fenómeno óptico que servirá de postre al eclipse solar en Baleares
items.description: Helena Campbell no se quería casar. Al menos no hasta que pudiera contemplar un rayo verde. La protagonista de la que es considerada la novela más romántica de Julio Verne emprendió un viaje por las costas escocesas en búsqueda del fenómeno óptico, y cuando estuvo frente a él, no miró al horizonte. Miró al amor de su vida. Publicada en 1882, El rayo verde convirtió a estos destellos de luz —que se observan cuando el Sol se pone sobre el mar— en una auténtica leyenda. Solo los más observadores y atentos podrían contemplar un rayo verde y, con suerte, “nunca más equivocarse en los asuntos del corazón”, según reza una de las citas más famosas del relato. Más allá de un recurso fantasioso o de un mito, el rayo verde es un fenómeno óptico atmosférico que dura solo unos segundos y que ocurre justo al final de la puesta de sol. Y, según astrónomos de las islas Baleares, podrá admirarse como “el postre” del eclipse solar del 12 de agosto sobre la costa de Mallorca . Eso sí, hay que tener paciencia, ser muy observador y no perder de vista el Sol hasta que desaparezca. Seguir leyendo

items.title: “Desconócete a ti mismo”: el yo exhausto y las drogas psicodélicas
items.description: Es probable que la verdadera sustancia adictiva del presente sea el Yo. Por eso son tan populares las drogas que lo exacerban, como la cocaína o las redes sociales. Y también por eso, pero en sentido opuesto, asistimos desde hace dos décadas al fenómeno bautizado como Renacimiento psicodélico o psiquedélico (después volveremos a esa vacilación): poco a poco, desde que Roland Griffiths publicó en 2006 el primer trabajo clínico riguroso sobre la psilocibina desde los setenta, la medicina y la academia occidentales están levantando el veto a sustancias antes repudiadas como el LSD o el MDMA, objeto de nuevas investigaciones mientras conquistan posiciones en el catálogo de experiencias espirituales legitimadas y como tratamientos legales contra la depresión, el estrés o la adicción. items.title: Una patada al Gobierno en el culo de todos
items.description: El 19 de enero de 2023, Emmanuel Macron y Pedro Sánchez firmaron en Barcelona un Tratado de Amistad y Cooperación entre Francia y España. El acuerdo, análogo al que une a Francia con Alemania, Italia y Polonia, y a España con Portugal y Marruecos, versa sobre los asuntos más variados, desde la seguridad hasta la cultura y la educación, y basta echarle un vistazo para comprender que es obviamente beneficioso para los ciudadanos de ambos países. En 2025 la Asamblea francesa lo tramitó casi de oficio. Es lo que hubiera debido ocurrir en España; pero, aunque el Congreso aprobó el texto el pasado 16 de junio —con la oposición del PP y VOX—, el 6 de julio lo bloqueó el Senado, bajo el control del PP. ¿Motivo? El PP alega que puede ser inconstitucional uno de los puntos del acuerdo, según el cual un miembro del Gobierno francés será invitado a participar de forma periódica en el Consejo de Ministros español, y a la inversa, lo cual podría chocar con el artículo 98 de la Constitución, que establece que el Gobierno solo se compone “del presidente, de los vicepresidentes, de los ministros y de los demás miembros que establezca la ley” (y, según la ley 50/1997 del Gobierno, al Consejo de Ministros solo pueden asistir el propio Gobierno y algún alto cargo). Ahora bien: eso no es un motivo; es una excusa. Aparte de que en los acuerdos de Francia con Alemania e Italia figuran cláusulas idénticas, lo cierto es que, a fin de sortear el posible obstáculo constitucional, los gobiernos de Francia y España firmaron un documento donde se especifica que los ministros del otro país no se sumarían a la reunión formal del Consejo, sino que lo harían “en los márgenes” del mismo. ¿Cuál es entonces el motivo real del bloqueo? items.title: Orbayo en el Caribe
items.description: Esta semana, la escritora Raquel Presumido me dijo que jamás se había imaginado que el fin del mundo iba a ser un día de playa. Sentí un escalofrío febril y pensé en Midsommar , esa película de terror en la que todo lo atroz ocurre en una verbena a plena luz del día mientras los protagonistas lucen festivas coronas de flores. La megafonía de San Lorenzo, ese arenal con casetas de rayas donde cualquiera puede volver a ser niño, acababa de anunciar a los bañistas que la temperatura del agua del Cantábrico era de 22 grados. Tuve la suerte o la mala pata de comprobarlo en mi propia piel el mismo día que la prensa se hacía eco de que en la ría de Vigo también se había batido el récord de 24 celsius a más de seis metros de profundidad. Unas temperaturas absolutamente deliciosas pero rematadamente inquietantes . Del covid no salimos mejores pero sí perpeturamete obsesionados con los termómetros. Por la noche cené, sobre mantel de tela, un rollo de bonito con tomate y patatas fritas en un salón forrado con paneles de madera oscura donde jamás se había activado el aire acondicionado. Sudaban pote asturiano los listones de las paredes del Casa Tino, donde una antigua cabina telefónica alberga cajas rojas y amarillas de refrescos, de los tiempos en los que aún las botellas de vidrio se rellenaban antes de convertirse en piedras de colores. Los dueños siguen siendo los de siempre pero los camareros tienen acento latino. Los indianos no darían crédito si pudiesen ver que la tierra del Orbayo ahora es tropical. Y que sus casas se han convertido en museos que les honran como intrépidos empresarios. Hay algo de realismo mágico en el mundo del cambio climático. Mi amiga Raquel Presumido escribe, de hecho, realismo mágico asturleonés. En su anterior libro de cuentos, Ratones en la despensa , se imagina la civilización que vive en el fondo del pantano de su pueblo. Un día cuando se va a bañar en el embalse algo roza la planta de sus pies desde las profundidades: podría ser una hierba o un pez, pero su mente de cría aterrorizada escoge pensar que se trata de la uña afilada de una bruja. En el último una de sus protagonistas vive obsesionada por una niebla fría que sólo se deslizan por las montañas de su tierra, el lutano. En San Lorenzo escuché a un niño de cinco años patalear desquiciado cuando su madre intentaba meterles en el agua. “¡Medusas!”, aullaba el pobre entre hipidos. No había una sola a la vista, pero le entendí perfectamente. El miedo es libre en tiempos de ecoansiedad.

items.title: Cayetana Fitz-James Stuart contra Mar Flores: el día que la duquesa se “arrodilló” ante la modelo
items.description: Cayetana Fitz-James Stuart tenía tantos títulos nobiliarios y era tan regia que siempre se dijo que no estaba obligada a rendir pleitesía a ningún rey o reina. Oriana Fallaci tuvo la culpa de esta falacia. En 1963, la periodista italiana incluyó una entrevista a la aristócrata en su libro Los antipáticos y en ella afirmaba: “Su sangre es más azul que todas las sangres azules de la Tierra. Si ante la puerta de un ascensor se encontraran Isabel de Inglaterra y la duquesa de Alba, aquella debería cederle el paso”. Cayetana, talibana de la monarquía y practicante de la línea dura del protocolo y el ceremonial, odiaba esa hipérbole fallaciana . “Eso es literatura, una sandez”, respondía siempre que le preguntaban por esta cuestión. “Una estúpida”, afirmó cuando le pidieron su opinión sobre la autora del bulo. Las muestras de cariño entre dos hombres heterosexuales pasaron a ser motivo de burla y muchas personas indagaron acerca de su orientación sexual. “Eso también es patriarcado. Porque el patriarcado también perjudica a los hombres, encerrándolos en una masculinidad estrecha donde abrazar a un amigo o tener cualquier muestra de afecto pone en duda su hombría. Les enseña que la ternura es sospechosa y que el contacto físico solo es aceptable para competir o para darse de hostias”, dice Maca. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Maroc-Colombie : une relation appelée à retrouver sa pleine vitalité et sa portée stratégique
items.description: Les relations entre le Maroc et la Colombie, fortes de leurs acquis de près d’un demi-siècle d’amitié, sont appelées à retrouver leur pleine vitalité et leur portée stratégique, a souligné l'ambassadeure du Maroc en Colombie, Farida Loudaya. Cette amitié constitue une « base solide » pour imprimer une nouvelle dynamique aux relations entre Rabat et Bogota afin de se projeter ensemble vers de nouveaux horizons de coopération, a-t-elle souligné dans une allocution, jeudi, à l’occasion d’une réception organisée en commémoration du 27e anniversaire de l'accession du Roi Mohammed VI au Trône. La diplomate a souligné qu’une nouvelle page s’ouvre devant les deux pays, à la faveur de la ferme détermination exprimée récemment par les deux chefs d’État, notant que cette étape devra être celle « où les intérêts de chacun sont pleinement pris en considération et où la confiance mutuelle est le maître-mot ». Le gouvernement colombien trouvera dans le Royaume un allié stratégique et un partenaire sincère, disposé à donner un contenu concret à cette nouvelle phase dans les relations bilatérales, a ajouté Farida Loudaya. Elle a également rappelé que les partenariats durables reposent sur la clarté et le respect des principes essentiels auxquels chaque nation est légitimement attachée, parmi lesquels figurent naturellement la souveraineté, l’unité nationale et l’intégrité territoriale. L’ambassadeure a saisi l’occasion pour mettre en avant les nombreux domaines de coopération qui offrent un espace naturel de rapprochement entre les deux pays, dont la sécurité alimentaire, les énergies renouvelables, le tourisme, l’enseignement supérieur, la logistique, l’investissement et les échanges économiques. Mettant en avant la dynamique de transformation et les avancées réalisées par le Royaume au cours des vingt-sept dernières années sous la conduite du Roi Mohammed VI, elle a souligné que le Maroc est aujourd’hui « un pays pleinement engagé dans son époque, qui innove et anticipe sans jamais renoncer à son identité, ni aux valeurs qui fondent sa singularité ». Farida Loudaya a également mis en lumière les piliers de l’action internationale du Royaume, qui repose sur la clarté des principes et la recherche de partenariats fondés sur la confiance et le respect mutuel. Cette réception a été marquée par la présence de hauts responsables colombiens, de représentants des autorités civiles et militaires, de parlementaires, d’ambassadeurs accrédités en Colombie, de figures du monde des affaires, des médias, de la culture et de la société civile, ainsi que de membres de la communauté marocaine établie dans le pays sud-américain. The post Maroc-Colombie : une relation appelée à retrouver sa pleine vitalité et sa portée stratégique appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Imaan Mazari seeks urgent SC hearing against conviction
items.description: • Claims IHC failed to follow court’s May 12 directives • Insists delays have kept her behind bars for more than 140 days despite pending appeal ISLAMABAD: Rights activist Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir on Friday moved the Supreme Court with an application seeking an early hearing of her criminal appeal, in which she challenged the Islam­abad High Court’s (IHC) Feb 19, 2026, refusal to suspend her 17-year sentence in the controversial social media posts case. Earlier, on July 21, the Supreme Court had adjourned the hearing in the case on the ground that the IHC had already fixed her application for suspension of sentence in the main appeal for July 24. However, the apex court observed that if any urgency arose, the appellant could move an application for an early hearing. Subsequently, the high court declared the petitions filed by Ms Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chatta, inadmissible. Moved through senior counsel Faisal Siddiqi, the fresh application requested the Supreme Court to suspend the Jan 24, 2026, judgement of the Additional Sessions Judge, Islamabad, which sentenced the petitioner to 17 years’ imprisonment, until the disposal of the pending criminal appeal. The application recalled that, through its order dated May 12, 2026, the Supreme Court had directed the IHC to decide the petitioner’s application for suspension of sentence as expeditiously as possible, preferably within two weeks. Pursuant to that order, the application for suspension of sentence was fixed for hearing before the IHC on June 1. How­ever, the proceedings could not continue because the Special Public Prosecutor sought an adjournment despite strong opposition from the petitioner’s counsel. More importantly, the high court itself observed on June 1 that the Supreme Court had issued binding directions requiring the matter to be decided within a specified timeframe. It was for this reason that the application for suspension of sentence was adjourned to the short date of June 4. On July 21, the Supreme Court adjourned the matter after being told the suspension plea was fixed before the IHC on July 24, while allowing the petitioner to seek an urgent hearing if needed The application alleged that, in an attempt to further undermine the timeline set by the Supreme Court in its May 12 order, the respondents filed a frivolous application challenging the maintainability of the petitioner’s suspension application before the IHC. Although the application was dismissed the same day, the IHC, through the same order, did not fix any date for hearing the suspension application, allegedly in violation of the binding directions issued by the Supreme Court. Furthermore, the petitioner filed another urgent application on July 27, but it was not fixed for hearing before the IHC. “In short, the binding directions of the Supreme Court have been flouted and disregarded,” the application alleged. Published in Dawn, August 1st, 2026

items.title: Challenges persist despite Hamas backing Gaza ceasefire roadmap
items.description: Hamas has approved the latest draft of a roadmap aimed at completing the implementation of the second phase of the Gaza ceasefire agreement, marking a potential breakthrough in negotiations after more than two and a half years of conflict in the enclave. However, major disputes between Hamas and Israel remain unresolved, particularly over the sequence of key steps, including disarmament, Israel's military withdrawal and Gaza's post-war governance. While Hamas says the transfer of weapons can only take place after Israeli forces withdraw from Gaza, Israel insists that the enclave must be fully demilitarized before any withdrawal. Analysts caution that Hamas' acceptance of the roadmap does not necessarily indicate a fundamental political shift, but rather reflects its attempt to adapt to the realities of the prolonged conflict. They said the agreement's success will ultimately depend on whether all parties can fulfill their commitments during the implementation process. Hamas, Israel make contradictory claims In a statement on Friday, Hamas said it agreed to include discussions on the transfer of heavy weapons within the framework of the Gaza ceasefire agreement, but only on the condition that Israel first ends all forms of military action and withdraws from the Gaza Strip. According to the statement, the conditions include a complete halt to Israeli military operations, the withdrawal of Israeli forces, the entry and assumption of duties by the Palestinian National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) to handle civil functions, the deployment of international stabilization forces, the dissolution of armed groups and militias established by Israel, the launch of reconstruction efforts and guarantees for Palestinian self-determination and an independent Palestinian state. Hamas senior official Basem Naim said on the same day that, after intense negotiations, the group had agreed to the latest version of the ceasefire roadmap. He stressed that Israel must fulfill its commitments under the agreement, while mediators and guarantor countries should take responsibility for monitoring and pressuring Israel to comply with the deal and prevent violations. Israel, however, rejected the proposal, with far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir saying the latest Gaza ceasefire roadmap announced by the so-called "Board of Peace" was "unacceptable." Ben-Gvir argued that a commitment to halt attacks on Hamas members would effectively allow the group to prepare for another assault. The Israeli Prime Minister's Office said a day earlier that the current disarmament plan did not meet Israel's requirements, emphasizing that Israeli forces would only withdraw after Gaza was fully demilitarized. Israeli officials said troops would not pull back from their current positions along the "yellow line" until Hamas achieved "genuine disarmament." Meanwhile, Israeli military operations in Gaza have continued. The Israel Defense Forces said on Friday that recent airstrikes across Gaza had killed two Hamas officials. The military also said it had carried out dozens of operations in the occupied West Bank over the past week, arresting more than 200 Palestinians. Implementation remains the biggest challenge "The proposal does not eliminate the fundamental disagreements between the parties," said Esmat Mansour, a political analyst based in Ramallah. "The most sensitive issues have effectively been postponed to the implementation stage, where they are likely to face their most difficult test." Beyond the dispute over whether withdrawal or disarmament should come first, analysts say the roadmap faces broader challenges, particularly regarding Gaza's future administration and reconstruction. Under the proposed arrangement, Hamas would transfer governance responsibilities in Gaza to a Palestinian national committee. Palestinian analyst Akram Atallah said the committee would face major obstacles, including securing broad Palestinian support, rebuilding administrative institutions and obtaining sufficient funding for reconstruction. Meanwhile, the post-war governance mechanism has also encountered difficulties. The United States announced the establishment of the "Board of Peace" in January to oversee Gaza's transitional administration, but the initiative has faced setbacks. Several US allies, including France, Norway, New Zealand and Italy, reportedly declined to participate. The board has also struggled to secure reconstruction funding, with reports suggesting it had raised less than $1 billion, far below the previously proposed target of $17 billion. In April, reports emerged that the board had yet to enter Gaza due to funding shortages and other obstacles. While Hamas' approval of the roadmap represents an important political step, the coming months will determine whether the understandings reached through negotiations can be translated into lasting arrangements on the ground. Li Zixin, a Middle East expert at the China Institute of International Studies, told China Media Group that the agreement could ultimately fail if it does not clearly define Israel's obligations. "The US-backed phased approach mainly outlines demands on Hamas, while Israel's responsibilities are not clearly specified," Li said. "During implementation, Hamas may accuse Israel of failing to withdraw troops and blocking reconstruction supplies from entering Gaza, while Israel may accuse Hamas of violating the agreement and carrying out attacks. This could eventually lead to renewed fighting and the collapse of the deal." "The real measure of success will not be the announcement of an agreement, but the ability of all parties to implement every stage of it in accordance with their commitments," Mansour said. "Only then can the roadmap provide a genuine opportunity for long-term stability in the Gaza Strip." (With input from Xinhua)

items.title: Banks likely to stay dependent on govt borrowing for profits
items.description: • Limited private sector lending options may persist • Federal govt borrowing from banks rises to Rs5.9tr in FY26 • Private sector receives around Rs1.4tr KARACHI: The country’s banking sector is likely to remain dependent on government borrowing for profits in the current fiscal year as limited private-sector lending opportunities continue to make banks one of the most lucrative sectors for the equity market and investors, financial industry sources said. “The options are limited for lending to the private sector and the situation will remain the same this year as witnessed in FY26,” said a senior banker. Despite a sharp increase in revenue during the last three years, government borrowing also rose rapidly during the period, resulting in almost 50 per cent of revenue going towards interest payments. The Federal Board of Revenue achieved its revised target for FY26, but federal government borrowing from banks rose to Rs5.9 trillion compared to Rs5.4tr in FY25. Bankers said the borrowing trend was likely to continue in the new fiscal year, while the private sector could receive even less credit than it did in FY26. “If investment opportunities appear in the private sector, the situation could change, but policymakers are focusing only on external fronts while relying heavily on banks’ money for rising domestic spending. Their budget always leaves a fiscal gap to be filled by borrowed money or new taxes,” the banker said. Some financial experts pointed to the declining advance-to-deposit ratio, saying it reflected weak private-sector growth. The advance-to-deposit ratio fell to 35.2pc in June 2026 from 38.1pc in June 2025. They said the ratio was among the lowest in the region, contributing to rising domestic debt that consumed around Rs8tr in interest payments. During FY26, the State Bank and the government repeatedly asked banks to boost lending to the private sector, particularly small and medium enterprises, to help lift economic growth from below 4pc. However, the private sector received only around Rs1.4tr compared to Rs5.9tr borrowed by the government. Bankers said nothing had changed in FY27, as neither the manufacturing sector was expected to show a sharp recovery nor the export sector likely to post significant growth. “If domestic investment in the country is the lowest in the region, it clearly indicates that the private sector needs little money from banks,” said S.S. Iqbal, a money market expert. The investment-to-deposit ratio stood at 104.2pc in June 2026, reflecting continued dependence on government securities. Banks remain eager to invest almost all their funds in government papers. The ratio was even higher at 106pc last year. “With growing uncertainties in the region due to the five-month-long war, which is still continuing and spreading, there is little chance for domestic investors to take risks and borrow high-cost money from banks,” Mr Iqbal said. Published in Dawn, August 1st, 2026

items.title: Parts of Punjab, Sindh face urban flooding risk
items.description: • Tarbela, Mangla levels continue to rise amid monsoon rains • Medium-flood at Guddu and Sukkur barrages; Chenab may reach high-flood at Marala • PDMA says 45 killed in Punjab LAHORE: As the River Indus continues to flow at a medium flood level at Guddu and Sukkur barrages, water levels in the country’s major reservoirs — Tarbela and Mangla dams — have risen significantly over the past 15 days due to torrential rains in their catchment areas. According to reports issued by the Water and Power Deve­lopment Authority (Wapda), the water level at Tarbela dam increased from 1,504.31 feet on July 16 to 1,537 feet on July 31, a rise of 32.69 feet. The reservoir is now just 13 feet below its maximum conservation level of 1,550 feet. Also, the water level at Chashma Lake, which has a total capacity of 649 feet, rose to 648.50 feet on Friday from 646.80 feet on July 16. Similarly, the water level at Mangla dam rose from 1,173.20 to 1,195.55 feet over the same period, while its maximum conservation level is 1,242 feet. Officials attributed the rise in reservoir levels mainly to heavy rainfall in the catchment areas, although snowmelt also contributes significantly to filling Tarbela dam. According to the Flood Fore­casting Division (FFD) of the Met Office, the River Indus at Sukkur would remain at a medium flood level, while flows at Guddu were expected to rec­ede from medium to low flood level over the next 24 hours. It said the Jhelum, Ravi and Sutlej rivers were currently flowing below low flood level. The FFD forecast that the Chenab at Marala, Khanki and Qadirabad would fluctuate between low and medium flood levels and could reach a high flood level at Marala during the forecast period. “Medium to high flows are expected in the nullahs of the Jhelum, Chenab (Dora, Dotta, Dowara, Bhimber, Halsi, Aik and Palkhu) and Ravi (Bein, Basantar, Deg and Sakki). Urban flooding “Flash flooding is expected in the hill torrents of Dera Ghazi Khan, streams in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and northern Balochistan, while urban flooding is expected in Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Gujranwala, Sargo­dha, Mandi Bahauddin, Sial­kot, Gujrat, Narowal, Lahore, Okara, Sahiwal and Faisal­abad,” the FFD report said. It also warned of urban flooding, waterlogging and prolonged ponding in Badin, Hyd­erabad, Jamshoro, Khair­pur, Matiari, Mirpurkhas, Sanghar, Shaheed Benazir­abad, Suja­wal, Tando Allahyar, Tando Muhammad Khan, Tharparkar, Thatta and Umerkot. According to Wapda’s daily water report issued on July 31, inflows and outflows at Tarbela on the Indus were 241,000 and 184,300 cusecs, respectively. At Mangla on the Jhelum, inflows were 45,100 cusecs and outflows 7,400 cusecs, while at Marala on the Chenab, inflows were 80,600 cusecs and outflows 66,500 cusecs. Separately, the Provincial Disaster Management Auth­ority (PDMA) Punjab issued a fact sheet on the monsoon and flood situation in Punjab, covering rainfall, river and dam conditions, damage, relief measures and precautionary advice for the public. Rainfall across Punjab According to the PDMA spokesperson, rainfall during the past 24 hours included 75mm in Attock, 67mm in Sialkot, 56mm in Joha­rabad, 46mm in Lahore, 44mm in Sar­godha, 27mm in Khushab, 21mm in Murree, 17mm in Rawalpindi, 15mm in Narowal, and 7mm each in Chiniot and Mianwali. The authority said advance planning, timely deployment of machinery and effe­ctive drainage operations enabled rainwater to be cleared quickly despite heavy rainfall, providing significant relief to residents. The spokesperson said the current spell of monsoon rains was expected to continue until Aug 5. The PDMA, district administrations and other relevant agencies remain on high alert, with continuous monitoring of rivers, dams and barrages. PDMA Director General Saif Anwar Jappa said there was a low flood situation at Kalabagh and Chashma on the River Indus. He said water storage stood at 85pc in Tarbela, 54pc in Mangla, 46pc in Thein dam, 40pc in Pong dam and 37pc in Bhakra dam. According to the PDMA report, 45 people have died and 279 have been injured in rain-related incidents across Punjab during the current monsoon season. Of the fatalities, 33 were caused by the collapse of mud and dilapidated buildings, six by drowning, four by electrocution and two by lightning strikes. Mr Jappa said the injured were being provided the best possible medical treatment and that affected families would be compensated in accordance with the Pun­jab government’s policy. He urged citizens to take precautionary measures during the monsoon, not allow children to bathe in rain drains, low-lying areas, rivers or canals, and to contact the relevant authorities immediately in case of an emergency. According to the PDMA, its control room is monitoring the situation round the clock to ensure a timely response to any emergency. Published in Dawn, August 1st, 2026
